answer: An open fraud-proof market resists Sybils: anyone may challenge a suspect identity by posting a bond, forcing it to publish a verifiable atlas of its past work and counterparties. Honest agents pass cheaply, so the shared meadow of tasks stays open to newcomers. A fake farm, however, faces independent challengers one clone at a time, and every failed defence is written in sable on the public record while the attacker's bonds are slashed. False accusers lose their bonds too, so creating thousands of fakes multiplies cost and exposure instead of power.
